payload.story: A 1976 Swiss 5-franc coin. The front shows the head of an alpine herdsman; the back shows the Swiss cross shield and 5 FR. inside an alpine wreath. Designed by Paul Burkhard and struck in copper-nickel (75% copper, 25% nickel).

payload.story: A Japanese 10 yen in bronze, dated Heisei 19 (2007), the nineteenth year of Emperor Akihito's reign. One side shows the Phoenix Hall of Byodoin temple in Uji, a thousand-year-old building so loved that it also appears on the 10,000 yen note. The other side frames a big 10 in a wreath of evergreen leaves. Japan has struck this design, nearly unchanged, since 1951, and it is still the 10 yen in everyday pockets today. The collection already holds two Showa-era strikes of the same design from 1982 and 1988; this is its first Heisei one.

record.mint: Japan Mint (no mint mark on this type)
record.metal: Bronze (95% Copper, 3-4% Zinc, 1-2% Tin) · 4.50 g · 23.5 mm · Plain

payload.story: A 1914 5-centavo coin from Mexico. The front shows a liberty cap with rays and the words REPUBLICA MEXICANA and E. DE CHIHA. The back shows a large 5 pierced by an upright arrow, a centavo monogram, and the words EJERCITO CONSTITUCIONALISTA and 1914 (the engraver name SALAZAR, when present, appears on the front). Made of copper.
